title: Interreligious dialogue: how to speak, listen and bear witness
tagline: Learn the Church's way of dialogue: truth with respect, proclamation with listening, and courage for mission.
whyItMatters: The Church tells us to meet people of other faiths with respect and to tell them about Christ. Both are needed, and they are not in conflict.

mindset.tip: Dialogue is not giving up your beliefs. It begins with respect and honest listening (Nostra Aetate 2; Ecclesiam Suam).
Dialogue and proclamation belong together. Neither replaces the other (Dialogue and Proclamation).
Do not confuse praying together with praying side by side. Read what Assisi actually was.
Look first for shared goods: the person, peace, the poor, family and creation (CCC 842-844).
Remember the martyrs who loved their neighbours of other faiths and stayed to the end.

resources.title: Ecclesiam Suam
resources.creator: Paul VI
resources.why: The encyclical that made dialogue a way of the Church: its model of concentric circles and its call to listen first.

resources.title: Dialogue and Proclamation
resources.creator: Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue and Congregation for the Evangelization of Peoples
resources.why: Shows how dialogue and proclaiming Christ belong together, with four forms of dialogue.

resources.title: Address to Representatives of the Churches and World Religions (Assisi 1986)
resources.creator: John Paul II
resources.why: What the first Assisi day of prayer for peace was and was not: praying side by side, not together.

resources.title: Fratelli Tutti
resources.creator: Francis
resources.why: Chapter 8 on religions in the service of fraternity in the world.

resources.title: Redemptoris Missio
resources.creator: John Paul II
resources.why: Why the Church still goes on mission, and how that fits with respect for other religions.

resources.title: Nostra Aetate: Declaration on the Relation of the Church to Non-Christian Religions
resources.creator: Second Vatican Council
resources.why: The Church's short foundation text: what is true and holy in other religions, and why Christians must reject hatred.
resources.note: Church teaching; paragraph 3 is on Muslims, paragraph 4 on Jews

resources.title: Is Heaven ONLY for Catholics?
resources.creator: Fr. Mike Schmitz
resources.why: A friendly answer to whether Catholics think only they are saved.

resources.title: Evangelii Gaudium
resources.creator: Francis
resources.why: Read paragraphs 250-254 on interreligious dialogue, including the passage on Islam.
resources.note: Church teaching (2013); long document, read the named section

resources.title: Lumen Gentium: Dogmatic Constitution on the Church
resources.creator: Second Vatican Council
resources.why: Read paragraph 16 on how those outside the visible Church are related to God's plan of salvation.

resources.title: Dominus Iesus
resources.creator: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith
resources.why: The Church's clear statement that Christ is the one Saviour, and why that is not contempt for others.

resources.title: Meeting for Peace in Assisi: Day of Reflection, Dialogue and Prayer
resources.creator: Benedict XVI
resources.why: Benedict's answer to worries about Assisi, and his call to be pilgrims of truth, including with non-believers.

resources.title: Document on Human Fraternity for World Peace and Living Together
resources.creator: Pope Francis and Grand Imam Ahmad al-Tayyeb
resources.why: A joint Catholic and Muslim statement; read it to see what the two leaders could say together.
resources.note: Joint statement (2019); a witness document, not a doctrinal definition

resources.title: Address to the Jewish Community of Rome (Synagogue, 13 April 1986)
resources.creator: John Paul II
resources.why: The first papal visit to a synagogue, where Jews are called "elder brothers" and anti-Jewish teaching is rejected.

resources.title: "The Gifts and the Calling of God Are Irrevocable" (Rom 11:29)
resources.creator: Commission for Religious Relations with the Jews
resources.why: A Vatican reflection on covenant, salvation and witness to Jews; useful for the hardest questions.
resources.note: Vatican commission reflection (2015); it says it is not a doctrinal teaching

resources.title: Faith, Reason and the University (Regensburg lecture)
resources.creator: Benedict XVI
resources.why: A famous lecture on reason, violence and God that shaped Catholic-Muslim dialogue afterwards.
resources.note: Papal lecture (2006); read with the Muslim reply "A Common Word"
